title: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference Through Weight Pruning and Quantization
problem: LLM inference is computationally expensive and memory-intensive. Achieving practical inference speedups while preserving model accuracy remains a key challenge.
motivation: Efficient LLM inference is critical for real-time deployment and reducing computational costs in production systems.
method: The method removes 40% of the model's weights (the numerical parameters that make predictions) while maintaining accuracy, then stores the remaining weights in 8-bit format (using fewer bits per number). Together, these cuts reduce the memory footprint and computation needed to run the model.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining pruning (removing unnecessary weights) with quantization (using fewer bits per number), optimized specifically for language models, to reach a 3.2x speedup in inference.
contributions: Pruning strategy achieving 40% weight removal with accuracy preservation in LLMs
Post-training 8-bit quantization compatible with pruned model weights
3.2x inference speedup on typical LLM workloads
Combined pruning-quantization framework for inference acceleration
limitations: Specific baseline systems and detailed accuracy metrics not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Accelerating LLM inference through weight pruning and quantization
